Alright, the latest run of the smoke test script produced a few console errors: three 404s for missing resources. The diagnostic snippet I just executed collected all missing URLs into a `missing` array and printed it; the output shows `["/favicon.ico"]`. That indicates the only missing resource is the favicon, and it's being requested three times (likely by the browser automatically on each navigation or refresh). The rest of the test appears to have succeeded: the logs show the progression through the game—starting at player-house, walking out, rival battle, catching a Pokémon, evolving it, and after reload the party reflects the evolved Pokémon. No other console errors were reported, so the test itself is functional.

Given the user wants to continue, I should address the 404s. The simplest fix is to provide a favicon file, or at least an inline data URI so the request doesn't 404. Adding an inline favicon directly in the HTML (e.g., a `<link rel="icon" href="data:image/png;base64,...">`) will satisfy the browser without needing an actual file on disk. That should eliminate the 404 logs.

After fixing the favicon, the next logical step is to verify the visual output of the test. The script saves screenshots into `tools/shots/`. The user likely wants to see those screenshots to confirm the UI looks correct. So I should tell them that I'm adding an inline favicon, then propose to show the screenshots. This aligns with the pattern: first acknowledge the only error (favicon), explain the fix, and then move on to the next verification step (visual inspection).

Thus, the appropriate response is a brief message stating that the only missing resource is the favicon (logged three times), that I'll add an inline one, and then ask to view the screenshots.
